Two call sites — that's not the threshold yet. Rule of Three: I'd wait for a genuine third occurrence before extracting a shared helper.

The reason isn't just "rules say so" — with only two examples, you're guessing at what the shared shape should actually be. Same backoff intervals? Same retry count? Same exception types getting caught? If those details differ even slightly between the two call sites, an abstraction built now bakes in the wrong shape, and untangling it later costs more than the duplication would have.

So: name it, note where the two live, and if a third shows up, propose the helper then — at that point you'll actually have enough data to know what it needs to look like.

Is there a third one already lurking, or is it genuinely just the two right now?
